title: Concavity from changing average rates of change
body: When the average rate of change over equal-length input-value intervals is increasing for all small-length intervals, the graph is concave up; when it is decreasing for all small-length intervals, the graph is concave down.
ced_evidence: 1.3.B.3: "When the average rate of change over equal-length input-value intervals is increasing for all small-length intervals, the graph of the function is concave up." (also 1.1.B.3, 1.1.B.4, 1.4.A.5)

title: Image and preimage
body: The image of an input value is the single output value yielded by the function rule, and the preimage of an output value is the set of input values for which the function rule yields that output value.
ced_evidence: 1.1.A.2: "The image of an input value is the single output value yielded by the function rule. The preimage of an output value is the set of input values for which the function rule yields that output value." (also 1.12.A.5)

title: Polynomial function in standard form
body: p(x)=a_n x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+a_{n-2}x^{n-2}+\cdots+a_2x^2+a_1x+a_0,\quad n \text{ a positive integer},\ a_i \text{ a real number for each } i \text{ from } 0 \text{ to } n,\ a_n\neq 0
ced_evidence: 1.4.A.1: "p(x) = a_n x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + a_{n-2}x^{n-2} + ... + a_2x^2 + a_1x + a_0, where n is a positive integer, a_i is a real number ... and a_n is nonzero"

title: Factored form vs. standard form
body: The factored form of a polynomial or rational function readily provides information about real zeros, and can therefore reveal information about x-intercepts, asymptotes, holes, domain, and range. The standard form can reveal information about end behavior.
ced_evidence: 1.11.A.1 and 1.11.A.2: "the factored form of a polynomial or rational function readily provides information about real zeros" / "The standard form ... can reveal information about end behaviors"

title: End behavior limit notation for polynomials
body: \text{For a nonconstant polynomial } p:\quad \lim_{x\to\infty}p(x)=\infty \text{ or } -\infty,\qquad \lim_{x\to-\infty}p(x)=\infty \text{ or } -\infty
ced_evidence: 1.6.A.1 and 1.6.A.2: "lim p(x) = ∞ or lim p(x) = -∞" as x → ∞ and as x → -∞; 1.6.A.3: degree and sign of the leading term determine end behavior
correction_note: product-owner-directed correction by the Claude session (David, 2026-10-10): the escalated row was corrected against its own CED evidence and re-checked by both independent checkers and the own-family veto

title: Location of a hole
body: \text{If the graph of a rational function } r \text{ has a hole at } x=c, \text{ and input values sufficiently close to } c \text{ give output values arbitrarily close to } L, \text{ then the hole is at } (c,L);\ \lim_{x\to c^-}r(x)=\lim_{x\to c^+}r(x)=\lim_{x\to c}r(x)=L
ced_evidence: 1.10.A.2: "the hole is located at the point with coordinates ( c , L ). The corresponding mathematical notation is lim r(x) = L"

title: Choosing a function type for a model
body: Match the function type to the pattern in the data or context, in the order the CED lists them.

items.label: Linear
items.meaning: Data or contexts that demonstrate roughly constant rates of change (1.13.A.1).

items.label: Quadratic
items.meaning: Data or contexts with roughly linear rates of change, or roughly symmetric data with a unique maximum or minimum value (1.13.A.2). Geometric contexts involving area or two dimensions can often be modeled by quadratic functions (1.13.A.3).

items.label: Cubic
items.meaning: Geometric contexts involving volume or three dimensions can often be modeled by cubic functions (1.13.A.3).

items.label: Polynomial of degree n
items.meaning: Data or contexts with multiple real zeros or multiple maxima or minima (1.13.A.4), or roughly constant nonzero nth differences (1.13.A.5).

ced_evidence: 1.13.A.1–1.13.A.7: "Linear functions model data sets or aspects of contextual scenarios that demonstrate roughly constant rates of change."

title: Additive and multiplicative transformations
body: The four transformation forms of f and the effect each has on the graph of f.

items.label: g(x) = f(x) + k
items.meaning: Additive transformation giving a vertical translation of the graph of f by k units (1.12.A.1).

items.label: g(x) = f(x + h)
items.meaning: Additive transformation giving a horizontal translation of the graph of f by -h units (1.12.A.2).

items.label: g(x) = a f(x), a ≠ 0
items.meaning: Multiplicative transformation giving a vertical dilation of the graph of f by a factor of a; if a < 0 the transformation involves a reflection over the x-axis (1.12.A.3).

items.label: g(x) = f(bx), b ≠ 0
items.meaning: Multiplicative transformation giving a horizontal dilation of the graph of f by a factor of 1/b; if b < 0 the transformation involves a reflection over the y-axis (1.12.A.4).

ced_evidence: 1.12.A.1–1.12.A.4: "g(x) = f(x + h) ... results in a horizontal translation of the graph of f by −h units"
